thread:
raj: Heads-up — after last night's maintenance I see a bunch of GPU slots still held by pods that are long gone, looks like orphaned allocations in gpu-pool-eu-west1.

nate: hmm, I saw a spike in Pending pods around 03:15UTC. Any logs from the allocator?

raj: allocator logs show: `lease grant` then no heartbeat from kube for those pod uids. suspect node reboots left stale leases.

sasha: can you paste `kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=redwood/gpu-slot`?

raj: sure — snippet:
```
NAME                      READY   STATUS    NODE                AGE
train-xyz-0               0/1     Pending   <none>              4h
inference-batch-12        0/1     Pending   <none>              4h
... (10 more)
```

marta: meanwhile `kubectl describe node gpu-node-17` shows the node is Ready but our allocator thinks it's drained. mismatch between kube scheduler and our pool inventory.

nate: ops-bot, can you run a pool resync for gpu-pool-eu-west1 and report diffs?

ops-bot: @channel starting resync for pool gpu-pool-eu-west1. Comparing cloud reservation state -> cluster inventory. Estimated 14 stale leases, 3 missing nodes.

raj: plan: (1) mark affected leases as reclaimed in allocator (safe), (2) trigger eviction guard for any live pod that actually occupies real GPU, (3) uncordon nodes we mistakenly flagged. Thoughts?

sasha: +1 but add a dry-run step to log which pod uids would be reclaimed to avoid hitting live jobs.

nate: Agree. Also let's throttle reclamation to 2 leases/sec to avoid bursty scheduler churn. Add a canary run in eu-west1a first.

marta: I'll prepare the command. ops-bot: run dry-run with canary flag. Command: `./allocator resync --pool gpu-pool-eu-west1 --dry-run --canary-az eu-west1a --rate 2/s`

ops-bot: Dry-run complete. Diff summary: 14 stale leases proposed for reclamation, 2 of those map to pods that are Terminating on kube (age 40m), 12 map to non-existent pods. No active container processes observed on nodes per cloud-agent.

raj: sounds safe. let's proceed with reclamation but exclude any Terminating pods until they finish. I'll trigger the actual resync now with `--exclude-terminating`.

ops-bot: Reclamation started: reclaiming leases (0/14)

nate: while this runs, can we add a temporary reconciler rule to bump lease heartbeat window from 90s -> 300s for maintenance windows, so we don't prematurely create churn next week?

sasha: yes but make it opt-in per-pool. We don't want relaxed windows globally.

marta: created PR to add pool-level heartbeat-window config + API flag. review: https://git.internal/redwood/alloc/PR/4321

ops-bot: Reclamation progress: 7/14 reclaimed, 0 evicted live pods, 0 failures.

raj: reclaimed 12 so far, two remaining are Terminating — waiting for kube to finish.

nate: once done, monitor scheduler latency and pending queue length for 30m. Post numbers here.

ops-bot: Done. Final: 12 stale leases reclaimed, 2 deferred (terminating). Pool capacity recovered ~28 GPUs, pending queue drained from 42 -> 6 in 18m.

raj: great. Action items: 1) rollout pool-level heartbeat config (marta) 2) add resync dry-run as a weekly cron for critical pools (nate) 3) update runbook with throttling guidance and canary az steps (sasha).

marta: I'll follow up with PRs and a short runbook snippet.

sasha: leaving a note to ops: if we see >5 stale leases in a pool after maintenance, auto-trigger dry-run and notify #eng-platform.

nate: +1. Thanks all. :tada:
